text:
lia: ticket INC-2024-1102 — backup vendor emailed that some nightly multipart uploads show up in the bucket without ServerSideEncryption. noticed by their checksum mismatch job at 04:11 UTC.
dev-bot: [alert] 4923456789: multipart-complete with missing SSE (parts_count=5, objects=3).
peter: can you paste the CloudTrail PutObject/CompleteMultipartUpload events? multipart parts are PutObject? parts are UploadPart calls.
tina: here's what we got from vendor logs, they use presigned UploadPart URLs and CompleteMultipartUpload from their controller: 
```
2024-12-02T04:10:23Z UploadPart requestId=abcd-1111 partNumber=1 x-amz-server-side-encryption=null
2024-12-02T04:10:24Z UploadPart requestId=abcd-1112 partNumber=2 x-amz-server-side-encryption=null
2024-12-02T04:11:01Z CompleteMultipartUpload requestId=efgh-2222 x-amz-server-side-encryption=null
```
lia: interesting — the CompleteMultipartUpload record lacks SSE too. S3 will only set object-level SSE if the parts were uploaded with SSE and the final request indicates it? I thought CompleteMultipartUpload can set it.
alex: CompleteMultipartUpload inherits the SSE header if present on parts or if included in the final Complete call. Looks like neither was present. vendor's presigned part URLs weren't signing the sse header so parts are uploaded without SSE.
peter: why did presigned URLs change behavior? we previously required presigned uploads to include x-amz-server-side-encryption header and signed it into the URL. tina: we rotated the presign service yesterday to the new CDN and a small middleware drop forgot to forward the sse header into the signed string. vendor didn't notice because large parts completed and checksums matched client-side, but our verify-run flagged absence of SSE on object metadata.
lia: blast radius — vendor said 3 objects affected (3 tenants). any evidence objects were public or exfiltrated? alex: bucket ACLs are private, public access blocked, so exposure <-> unlikely. still classified as compliance P1 because at-rest encryption absent.
tina: quick mitigation: I can re-issue signed part URLs with SSE enforced and replay upload for the same keys, but parts already uploaded won't get retroactive SSE. we should re-encrypt final objects.
peter: re-encrypt plan: copy-object with --server-side-encryption aws:kms. For multipart objects we can do a single S3 Copy since S3 treats final object as whole. example: 
```
aws s3api copy-object --bucket redwood-snaps --key vendor/2024-12-02/obj1 --copy-source redwood-snaps/vendor/2024-12-02/obj1 --server-side-encryption aws:kms --ssekms-key-id alias/redwood-snaps-cmk
```
lia: runbook note — do this with rate limit and verify checksums afterwards. also produce a list of affected object keys and CloudTrail event IDs for the incident ticket.
alex: two immediate infra fixes: 1) patch presign service to include SSE in signed headers; 2) add bucket policy to Deny PutObject/UploadPart without SSE header. BUT caution: UploadPart cannot be denied by s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption condition on the UploadPart call? we need to test.
peter: UploadPart operations accept headers but the bucket policy condition key is s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption which applies to UploadPart and PutObject, afaik. snippet to deny non-KMS: 
```
{
  "Sid": "DenyNonKMSSSE",
  "Effect": "Deny",
  "Principal": "*",
  "Action": ["s3:PutObject","s3:UploadPart"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::redwood-snaps/*",
  "Condition": {"StringNotEquals": {"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"}}
}
```
lia: make this a short-term guardrail but coordinate with vendor for presign rollout within the maintenance window.
tina: will push presign hotfix now, then regenerate presigned URLs for the delayed multipart flows. ETA 30m.
alex: another angle — KMS grants: vendor role had an ephemeral grant scoped with aws:RequestTag for tenant_id, but presigned flows don't send RequestTag on UploadPart. Grant didn't match, so parts may have been uploaded unencrypted even earlier in the chain? Wait we see no kms:Encrypt failures in CloudTrail — it's just unset header. Means requests didn't present SSE header so KMS not involved. If we later rely on grants with RequestTag they won't help if header absent. We should adjust grant to principal+resource ARNs instead of request-tag condition.
peter: agree. change CMK grant pattern: principal=arn:aws:iam::111:role/vendor-uploader + resource constraint on key policy to authorize Encrypt for that principal. Avoid brittle request-tag conditions for presign flows.
ulia: (typo) lia: also add a CI test that creates a small multipart flow using presigned UploadPart URLs and asserts object SSE metadata after completion.
tina: operational cleanup: re-encrypting 3 objects now. replaying two of them via CopyObject method. progress: 2/3 done.
peter: audit/forensics: we lost S3 server access logging during bucket migration last month, that's why detection was delayed to vendor checksum job. add to action items: re-enable access logging and lifecycle for logs.
lia: next steps logged in INC-2024-1102: 
- finalize re-encrypt and checksum verification (today)
- presign service hotfix and vendor rollout (30m)
- bucket policy deny non-kms (post-rollout)
- adjust CMK grant pattern + key policy audit (EOD)
- add multipart presign acceptance test in CI (tomorrow)
- re-enable server access logging and add CloudWatch metric alert for PutObject events without SSE (week)
tina: handing off to oncall vendor patch. I'll update ticket with list of keys and presign diffs. :thumbsup:
lia: thanks all. please attach CloudTrail IDs and the Verify-run alert logs to the ticket. we'll do a short postmortem next week.
